title: inspect_swarm
text:
A swarm of agents working on one sample.
Each member gets a timeline in the sample named after it, so member names must be unique across the swarm runs and other timelines in a sample. To run swarms more than once in one sample, build them with distinct member names. A member may not be named init, solvers or scorers: Inspect’s timelines read spans with those names as the sample’s phases.

Source

@agent
def swarm(
    members: Member | Agent | Sequence[Member | Agent],
    *,
    controller: str | Controller = "leaderless",
    channels: str | Channel | Sequence[str | Channel] = ("filesystem",),
    budget: Budget = Budget(),  # noqa: B008
) -> Agent

members Member | Agent | Sequence[Member | Agent]

The roster: built agents or member() records. A bare agent is member(agent). A factory-form member() may stand for several members (count).

controller str | Controller

How the swarm runs: who starts, when and with what input, and when the swarm is done. A name resolves to a registered controller with its default parameters.

channels str | Channel | Sequence[str | Channel]

How members share information. A name resolves to a registered channel with its default parameters. [] means none: members get no channel instructions, though a shared sandbox is still shared.

budget Budget

The swarm-wide cap.





A swarm member, with a name, role, limits or count.
A member is a built agent, member(react(prompt=...)), or a registered @agent factory and its arguments, member(deepagent, args={"tools": [bash()]}, count=4). Both must be registered with @agent, so that the log can name them and replay can find them. A built agent can also be passed to swarm(members=...) without member().
No agent object runs twice at the same time in one sample. A built agent is one member: it is built once, when the task is built, and shared by concurrent samples, as any Inspect solver is. The same agent object cannot be in two members. Several copies of one configuration (count above 1) need the factory form: the swarm calls factory(**args) once for each member in each sample, so each copy gets its own agent and whatever the factory builds. member() checks the arguments against the factory’s signature but does not call it, so the factory’s own checks run when the member is built.
Names. Members left on their default name are numbered across the whole roster, not per record, so one member with different arguments takes two records: [member(react, args={"prompt": a}, count=6), member(react, args={"prompt": b, "model": m})] is react-1 to react-7. When every copy differs, give each its own record, as in [member(react, args={"prompt": p}) for p in prompts]. Names given with name are not numbered across records, so give each record its own.
Objects given to an agent are shared. Every member built from one record receives the same objects from args, and two built agents given the same tool object share it, across members and samples. Inspect’s built-in tools keep their state in the sample store or the sandbox, so this matters only for a custom tool or helper that keeps state in its Python object (a counter, a cache, a client). To give each member its own, construct it inside a member builder, an @agent factory that builds the configured agent, and use the factory form.
Tool state. Each member runs in its own tool-state scope, named after the member. Built-in tools that keep state in the sample store (memory(), bash_session(), web_browser(), the skill tool) give each member its own state when their instance is left at the default, so the default memory() is private to each member. An explicit instance is used as given: members, or the copies of one counted member, that name the same instance share its state, so a board shared on purpose is memory(instance="board"). The sample store itself is shared. State that custom tools or agent code keep in the store with no instance is shared unless they resolve their instance with tool_state_instance(). Built-in tool state that a setup solver prepared at the default instance before the swarm runs is not visible to the members.
Submissions. A member that returns normally has submitted, and its output is its answer, unless the output’s stop reason is content_filter or model_length. That is how react() returns after three refusals or a context overflow it could not recover from, so the member ends unsubmitted and the swarm never chooses its output as the answer. Other agents keep the rule that a normal return is a submission: an agent that gives up in some other way and returns is treated as having answered.
Stopping itself. An agent that raises LimitExceededError("custom", ...) with no source to stop itself ends only its member, with status member_limit:custom; the other members continue and the swarm never chooses its output as the answer. This holds when the error is raised in a task group inside the agent, too.
Sandboxes. Members share the sample’s sandbox by default. With sandbox, a member works in its own: the swarm makes that environment the member’s default, so sandbox() in its tools returns it, and hides the sample’s other environments from the member except those in visible_sandboxes, such as a shared service. Tools that choose a sandbox without a name, such as text_editor(), bash_session() and the agent bridge, use the member’s own; a visible service is reached only by name. sandbox="{member}" gives each copy of a counted member the environment named after it: member(factory, name="agent", count=2, sandbox="{member}") runs agent-1 and agent-2 in the environments of those names. The sample’s sandbox configuration provides the environments (for Docker, a compose service for each), and the swarm checks that they exist when it starts. When one member has its own sandbox, every member must have one, no two the same, and the filesystem channel, which describes a shared sandbox, can be used only as filesystem(shared_volume=True), for sandboxes that each mount one shared volume. A service in visible_sandboxes is reachable from any of the member’s tools that take a sandbox name, so list only services every member may use.
Chosen names. With choose_name=True the member is not told its name: its preamble says how many agents are in the swarm and asks it to choose a name for itself and tell the other members, and the filesystem channel tells it to keep its work in a directory named with the name it chose. Its role, if it has one, is still stated. The swarm’s records, spans, tool-state scopes and budget shares still use name. A swarm in which any member chooses its name can use only the filesystem channel or no channel (channels=[]), since other channels show members to each other by name. Text you give the member yourself is not changed: the sample input, a controller’s start(input=...), the agent’s prompt and the sandbox configuration.
Scoring with member sandboxes. The task’s scorers run after the swarm, outside every member, where sandbox() is default. A scorer that grades the members’ work names each member’s sandbox itself, as in sandbox("agent-1"), and the sandbox field of each member in the swarm’s result record says which member used which.
Background work belongs to the member. Work its agent starts with background(), such as deepagent(background=...) subagents, spends through the member’s limits and share, and is the member’s in the ledger. When the member’s agent returns, the swarm stops the background work from starting model calls, gives it the swarm’s grace period to finish calls and tool calls in flight, and cancels what is left. The member ends after that, with the status its agent ended with; Budget.grace=0 cancels background work at once. A member time limit bounds its agent only: after the agent returns, its background work gets the grace period too, and the cancelled work’s cleanup is awaited. Background work must be started by the agent while it runs; a factory that starts it while building the agent makes the member errored. A sourceless custom limit error raised in background work ends only the task that raised it; the member’s agent and its other background work continue. Work started outside background() (an asyncio task, a process left running in the sandbox) is not stopped. Bridged members cannot have background work: background() raises in a member declared or found bridged, and a member that uses the agent bridge after starting background work (through a bridged subagent, for example) is cancelled and ends errored.
ACP agents, which wait for their caller to drive them rather than returning, are refused: a built one when member() is called, and a factory’s when the member is built.

text:
Controllers

leaderless
Start every member with the swarm’s input; stop at the first submission, or when all have ended.
By default the swarm stops when the first member submits. The swarm’s answer is the first submission, so nothing the other members do after it can change the answer. The members still running are stopped: they finish the calls they have in flight, within Budget.grace, and the ones still running after it are cancelled.
Pass stop_on_submission=False to let every member run to its end when the other members’ work still matters: tasks whose scorer reads a shared artifact (such as the sandbox) after the members end, where members still working change what is scored; arms that measure each member’s result (team@k); and agents for which any normal return counts as a submission, so that a member that gives up would end the swarm. Add final="last" to make the latest submission the answer, for a team whose members build on each other’s work.

Channels

filesystem
A shared directory, with a convention for using it, stated in each member’s preamble.
By default the channel describes the sample’s sandbox, which the members share: a directory for shared files, a notes file members append to, and a scratch directory for each member.
With shared_volume=True it describes members with their own sandboxes (member(sandbox=...)) that each mount one shared volume at shared: shared and the notes file in it are the same directory in every member’s sandbox. There is no scratch directory, since each member’s sandbox is already its own. The swarm cannot check that the volume is mounted in every member’s sandbox; it takes your word for it.
The channel adds no tools and does not create the directories.

Source

@swarm_channel
def filesystem(
    shared: str = "/shared",
    notes: str = "notes.md",
    scratch: str = _SCRATCH,
    shared_volume: bool = False,
) -> Channel

shared str

The directory for files members share. With shared_volume=True, an absolute path where the volume is mounted.

notes str

The notes file members read and append to, relative to shared (or an absolute path). With shared_volume=True it must be inside shared.

scratch str

Each member’s own directory. {member} is replaced by the member’s name. For a member that chooses its own name, {member} is shown as <your name>, and when any member chooses, no member is told its directory is unused. Not used with shared_volume=True.

shared_volume bool

Whether members have their own sandboxes that each mount one shared volume at shared. swarm() accepts the channel beside per-member sandboxes only with True, and refuses True when members share the sample’s sandbox.




shared_memory
A board of files that every member of the swarm, and their subagents, read and write.
Each member gets a shared_memory tool with the commands and parameters of inspect_ai’s memory() over files under /shared_memory. Every write goes through the swarm’s bus as a record from the member that made it. A view shows a file inside a fence that names its last writer and version, and lists of changed files name them by ids such as f-3, which view takes as its file_id. A loop must view a file in its current version before it overwrites it with create, inserts into it, renames it or deletes it. append needs no view: it adds text on a new line at the end of a file, creating the file if it does not exist. changes returns only the list of files other agents changed since the loop last viewed them, which ends every result. That list names at most 10 files at the end of a result, and every file in changes.
A fence is a label for the reader, not a protection: a member can write text that looks like a fence, another member’s file or a status line.
The board lives for one run of the swarm. A result longer than the tool output limit is truncated in the middle, as Inspect truncates any tool’s result.
Each member, and each of its subagents, also gets swarm_wait, which blocks until a file it watches has a change it has not viewed, another member ends, every member is waiting, the swarm stops, or a timeout passes. A wait is wall-clock time inside a tool call: it counts towards the member’s time limit, the swarm’s time cap, and the sample’s time and working limits. It makes no model call, so it adds no tokens, cost or steps.

Source

@swarm_channel
def shared_memory(
    max_files: int = 10_000,
    max_file_bytes: int = 1_000_000,
    max_file_lines: int = 100_000,
    max_board_bytes: int = 100_000_000,
    rate: tuple[int, float] | list[int | float] | None = (60, 60.0),
    max_wait: int = 600,
) -> Channel

The most files on the board, at least 1.

max_file_bytes int

The most UTF-8 bytes in one file, at least 1.

max_file_lines int

The most lines in one file, at least 1.

max_board_bytes int

The most UTF-8 bytes in all files together, at least max_file_bytes.

rate tuple[int, float] | list[int | float] | None

The most writes one member may make, all its loops together, in a sliding window of seconds, as (count, seconds); None for no limit.

max_wait int

The longest swarm_wait in seconds, at least 1, and its default timeout.




messages
Direct messages between the members of the swarm.
Each member’s own loop gets three tools. send_message sends a message to a member, to several, or to "all", every other running member, and returns its id, such as m-3. read_messages returns the member’s unread messages, oldest first, each inside a <peer_message> fence that names its id, sender and recipients, and marks them read. list_members lists the roster with each member’s role, state and, once it has ended, its status. While a member has unread messages, the results of send_message, list_members, shared_memory and swarm_wait in its own loop end with a line that counts them; list_members also says when there are none. The tools of other channels carry no count. Nested loops, such as a deepagent() member’s subagents, get none of these tools, so a member’s inbox has one reader.
Every send goes through the swarm’s bus as a record from the member that made it. A send is refused when an address is not a running member other than the sender, when the message is empty or longer than max_bytes, when a recipient already has max_unread unread messages, when the sender is over its rate, or, with dedupe, when a recipient still has the same text from the same sender unread. A refused send reaches no recipient.
One read always returns at least the oldest unread message whole: the read is bounded by the largest fence the roster allows plus max_bytes, and Inspect’s tool output limit does not apply to it.
A fence is a label for the reader, not a protection: a member can write text that looks like a fence, another member’s message or a status line.
The member’s own loop also gets swarm_wait, which returns while it has unread messages sent with wake=True (the default), and otherwise blocks as shared_memory()’s does, up to max_wait seconds. A wait is wall-clock time inside a tool call: it counts towards the member’s time limit, the swarm’s time cap, and the sample’s time and working limits.
The channel needs member names that start with a lowercase letter, followed by at most 47 lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, other than all and swarm. Bridged members cannot use it yet.

The tools of the swarm’s channels, for a member’s agent.

title: inspect_swarm.analysis
text:
The ledger

swarm_ledger
Read the swarm’s ledger from a sample.

Source

def swarm_ledger(sample: EvalSample) -> SwarmLedger | None

sample EvalSample

A sample read from a log with its store, for example from read_eval_log(). A sample that runs two swarms keeps only the last one’s ledger.




SwarmLedger
Realized usage and cost of one run of the swarm, and how complete they are.
The swarm writes its ledger once, when it ends, to the sample store as inspect_swarm:ledger and as an InfoEvent with source inspect_swarm. Read it from a sample with swarm_ledger().
The store entry’s shape follows version. This inspect_swarm reads version 1 only.

Source

class SwarmLedger(BaseModel)

Attributes

version Literal[1]

Format version of the ledger.

budget Budget

The swarm’s budget as configured.

caps dict[str, float | None]

The swarm’s caps, derived or explicit, keyed by cost (dollars), tokens and time (seconds). None for a kind with no cap.

sample_limits dict[str, float | None]

The sample’s limits when the swarm started, keyed by token, cost, message, turn, working and time. None for a limit not set.

members list[MemberLedger]

Each member, in roster order.

runtime Meter

Calls made by the swarm’s runtime, such as the controller’s.

final Meter

Calls made by the final step, which chooses the answer.

swarm Meter

Every call in the swarm’s context: the members, the runtime, the final step and anything else.

calls Calls

Model events in the swarm’s span tree: the members, the runtime and the final step.

unpriced_calls_recorded int

Calls the swarm meter recorded with usage but no cost.

sample_delta ModelUsage

The sample’s model usage over the swarm’s lifetime, summed over its models.

unattributed ModelUsage

What the sample used over the swarm’s lifetime that the swarm meter did not record: tokens are sample_delta minus swarm.usage, and total_cost is sample_delta’s cost minus swarm.cost.

unpriced_models list[str]

Models in sample_delta with tokens but no cost.

native_compaction_classes list[str]

Loaded ModelAPI classes that override compact(), when the swarm started or ended. Native compaction emits no event, so the ledger cannot count its calls.

overshoot dict[str, float]

How far usage at the end went past each cap, keyed by cost, tokens and time. Only kinds over their cap appear.

stop_reason str | None

The reason the swarm stopped its members, from the first stop begun. None when no stop began.

ended_by str | None

The sample limit (sample_limit:<type>) or operator interrupt (operator) that ended the swarm, even during its own stop. unknown when an outside cause may have ended it but cannot be named. None when nothing from outside ended it.

interrupted bool

The swarm did not finish: an error, a limit or a cancellation ended it before or during its final step.

final_cancelled bool

The final step was cancelled.

resumed bool

The sample resumed from a checkpoint, so the swarm restarted its caps from zero. Swarms now refuse checkpointing, so only logs from earlier versions can have it true.

total_complete bool

No call is known to be missing from the swarm’s usage and cost: no member, member background task or final step was cancelled, the swarm was not interrupted, every call completed with priced usage, every model in sample_delta is priced, and no loaded model class compacts natively.

attribution_complete bool

total_complete, and the swarm meter recorded all the sample used over the swarm’s lifetime: unattributed is zero, to within rounding.





MemberLedger
One member’s entry in the swarm’s ledger.

Source

class MemberLedger(BaseModel)

Attributes

name str

The member’s name.

status str | None

How the member ended (submitted, swarm_cap, …), or None for a member never started.

bridged bool

The member runs a CLI agent through Inspect’s agent bridge.

meter Meter

Usage and cost of the calls made in the member’s context.

calls Calls

Model events in the member’s spans.

cancelled bool

The member’s agent was cancelled, or the swarm’s hard stop cancelled its background drain after the agent had returned. A hard stop during the drain keeps the agent’s status, so cancelled can be True with status="submitted". The agent is cancelled by the hard stop after a grace period, a member time limit or a cancellation from outside the swarm. A bridged member is also cancelled at once when it reaches a cap, its share or one of its own limits, or makes a call after the swarm stopped it.

background_started int

Tasks the member’s agent started with background(), such as deepagent() background subagents.

background_cancelled int

Of background_started, the tasks that were cancelled: still running when the member’s drain ended, or cancelled by an error from the member’s work or by the hard stop.





Meter
Usage and cost recorded by one of the swarm’s meters.
A meter counts the model calls made in its context: one member’s, the runtime’s, the final step’s, or the whole swarm’s.

Source

class Meter(BaseModel)

Attributes

usage ModelUsage

Token usage of the calls recorded, except those made while token metering was suspended (approval and review calls).

cost float

Cost in dollars of the priced calls recorded, suspended calls included.

suspended_cost float

The part of cost recorded while token metering was suspended (approval and review calls).





Calls
Counts of the model events in the swarm, or in one member’s spans.
errored, no_usage and unpriced count calls whose cost is missing, so any of them above zero makes the cost a lower bound.

Source

class Calls(BaseModel)

Attributes

calls int

Model calls that completed, cache replays excluded.

cache_replays int

Model events replayed from the cache (cache="read"). They cost nothing.

errored int

Model calls that ended in an error or were cancelled, plus the requests a provider’s client retried inside one call. Their usage is unknown.

no_usage int

Model calls that completed with output but no usage.

unpriced int

Model calls that completed with usage but no cost (total_cost is None).
